§6Plutonium Hexafluoride§f

§aThe plutonium equivalent of UF6. Corrosive, radioactive, gaseous. Fun stuff.§f

PuF6 is a corrosive radioactive gas that serves as the intermediary in plutonium enrichment. Unlike uranium, plutonium requires no additional processing to become a hexafluoride.

Production (Chemical Plant, 7.5s, 500HE/t): §e1,000mB§f Water + §bPlutonium Powder§f + §e3§f Fluorite = §e900mB§f PuF6.

Storage requires a specialized tank or Fluid Barrels. Processing: §bGas Centrifuge§f enriches PuF6 to separate Pu-238 from Reactor Grade Plutonium. The §bSILEX§f can further separate RGP into pure Pu-239 and Pu-240, skipping a step.

§cWARNING:§f PuF6 is corrosive, radioactive, and gaseous. Always wear full PPE.

§ePS:§f The SILEX is more efficient than the Gas Centrifuge for plutonium. It processes PuF6 directly and separates RGP into pure isotopes in one step.
